_about: Telemetry v2 event registry — the SINGLE source of truth for what may go
on the wire. Python (rapid_mlx/telemetry/registry.py) and Swift
(apps/rapid-mac/Sources/Rapid/Telemetry/TelemetryRegistry.swift) both read
THIS file; a pytest drift check asserts the Swift-bundled copy is
byte-identical, so the two cannot diverge.
Rules: every event property is an enum, a bool, a small bounded int, or a
model_id (pattern- and length-capped). There is no free-form string kind.
A breaking change (rename / re-mean / remove a key) needs a NEW event name;
additive OPTIONAL properties are safe in place.
Nothing in this file transmits on its own — see telemetry-design.md sec 4.
telemetry_model_id (design sec 1.3): the catalog alias when the model is
in aliases.json; else the public 'org/name' only when an anonymous Hub
fetch proved it public; else one of the reserved placeholders. Gated,
not-found, token-authenticated, local-path and --served-model-name values
are always '<custom>'. Never request.model. The pattern and the length cap
are defence in depth, not the classifier: the classifier lives in block 2.
The 'org/name' half mirrors redact._HF_REPO_RE.

surface._about: Design sec 1.2. Which Rapid component emitted the event.

channel._about: Design sec 1.2. Release channel of the running build.

os._about: platform.system().lower() as redact.platform_info() already reports it.

arch._about: platform.machine() as redact.platform_info() already reports it.

_about: Today redact._read_chip_brand() returns the raw sysctl brand string,
which is free-form and sec 1.5 forbids on the wire. This enum is the
closed vocabulary chip_tier.classify_chip_tier() already parses:
an M<generation> token crossed with VARIANT_BASE / _PRO / _MAX / _ULTRA.
'apple-other' covers an Apple chip whose generation is past this list;
'intel' covers Intel Macs; 'other' covers non-Darwin and unknown.

days_since_first_run_bucket._about: Design sec 1.2 cohort stamp — the veteran/newcomer split.

_about: Design sec 1.3, Orca's scale, reproduced exactly and in order. A bucket
event is a MILESTONE, not volume: the only valid chart is 'unique
installs that reached bucket >= N'. Summing these is meaningless.

bucket_source._about: Whether this process observed the crossing or found the bucket already reached.

result._about: Design sec 1.3, inference_bucket_reached. Counters are kept per outcome.

_about: Exactly telemetry/emit.py _ALLOWED_ENDPOINTS, which is already the
shipped allow-list for the v1 'request' event, plus 'other'. Anything
outside it collapses to 'other' — see emit._normalize_endpoint().
The label half of telemetry/redact.py _CALLER_AGENT_MARKERS, de-duped,
plus the two escape hatches normalize_caller_agent() already returns.
Block 2 adds X-Rapid-Client, which resolves to the SAME labels; the raw
User-Agent never leaves the machine (sec 1.5).
Derived from model_aliases._VALID_MODALITIES ({text, text-diffusion,
video-gen, image-gen, embedding}) with the alias flag
supports_image_input splitting 'text' into llm vs vlm — the loader
comment at model_aliases.py:183 states exactly that a VLM checkpoint
keeps modality='text'. 'vision' is in _RESERVED_MODALITIES (no dispatch
path yet) and is therefore NOT a separate value here.
There is no canonical quantization enum in the engine, so this is the
observed closed set of quant tokens carried by rapid_mlx/aliases.json
alias names and hf_paths, made canonical: ONE value per concept.
The catalog spells the same thing two ways ('granite-4.2-30b-4bit' vs
its 'granite-4.2-30b-q4-mlx' checkpoint, 'ltx-2.5-mlx-q8',
'cogvideox-fun-5b-q4'), so the 'q<n>' spelling is NORMALIZED to
'<n>bit' -- q2->2bit, q3->3bit, q4->4bit, q6->6bit, q8->8bit, and the
same for the dq<n> dynamic-quant family -- so q4/q8 and friends are
deliberately NOT values here. rapid_mlx/telemetry/quant.py:
quant_token() is the only normalization and every emitter must go
through it. THREE precedence rules when a name carries more than one
marker: (1) a SCHEME beats a width ('gpt-oss-20b-mxfp4-q8' -> mxfp4,
'...-4bit-dwq' -> dwq), or dwq/mxfp4 would be unreachable; (2) a
width beats a PRECISION ('qwen3.8-27b-4bit-fp16' -> 4bit, not fp16);
(3) 'other' also beats a precision ('...-awq-fp16' -> other), since
an unnamed quantization is still a quantization. So 'bf16'/'fp16'
mean 'no width AND no other quant-shaped token anywhere in the
name' -- (2) and (3) together are what keeps a quantized checkpoint
out of the not-quantized bucket.
'other' absorbs a quantization we have no canonical name for
yet so a fresh alias can never put an unknown token on the wire;
'unknown' means the name carries no quantization marker at all.
tests/test_telemetry_registry_drift.py walks the whole catalog
through quant_token() and fails if any name maps outside this enum.
Download footprint of the pulled checkpoint, bucketed. The design doc
names the property but not a scale, so this is a new log-ish GB scale
chosen to straddle the RAM tiers the recommender already reasons about
(8 / 16 / 32 / 64 GB). Half-open [lower, upper) like redact's buckets.

pull_source._about: Design sec 1.3 — which origin served the weights. Mirror health.

pull_error_class._about: Design sec 1.3, model_pull_failed. Verbatim from the table.

serve_error_class._about: Design sec 1.3, model_serve_failed. Verbatim from the table.

_about: Exactly the agent profiles `rapid-mlx agents` can configure — one YAML
per agent in rapid_mlx/agents/profiles/ (the same glob pyproject ships
as package-data), read from each profile's `name` field. Plus 'other'.
NOTE: the design doc's illustrative list names cursor and cline; those
are CALLER labels (they talk to the server), not configurable agent
profiles, so they are not here.
The failure modes rapid_mlx/agents/setup.py can actually reach:
no_safe_setup_flow  -> setup.py:230 'does not have a first-class safe setup flow'
config_invalid      -> setup.py:97 '<path> must contain a YAML mapping'
config_changed      -> setup.py:242/246 '<path> changed after preview'
config_write_failed -> an OSError out of the atomic-write / backup path
server_not_ready    -> setup.py:276 'server is not ready at <root>'
server_no_models    -> setup.py:280 'server at <root> reported no models'
model_not_advertised-> setup.py:282 'server does not advertise model ...'

reasoning/thinking controls, a Batch or Files API, blanket streaming.
Design sec 1.3. An env kill switch forbids all upload, so it is by
design unobservable and is NOT a value here.
Design sec 1.2 — stamped on EVERY event, validated by validate_common()
before the transport initialises (fail closed). Dropped vs. 0.14.3:
country (GeoIP is off), the dead 'engine' slot, the constant 'status'.
The two pattern-capped kinds ('version', 'uuid') exist only here; event
properties may not use them.

os_version._about: major.minor only — redact.platform_info() already truncates it.

memory_gb._about: redact.bucket_memory_gb() — rounded to whole GB, never exact bytes.

python_version._about: Engine surfaces only; the desktop app omits it.

nth_model_served._about: Cohort stamp: distinct models this install has EVER served, at emit time.

app_opened._about: Launches. Common props carry everything that matters.

_about: Once per install per UTC day, on the first successful inference — DAU
and retention that still work for a server that runs for weeks.
The design table writes 'surface' against this row; surface is already a
common prop on every event, so repeating it here would put the same key
on the payload twice. It is not duplicated.

model_pulled._about: What people want to run, and whether the mirror served it.

model_pull_failed._about: _failed twin: same identifying props, all optional, plus error_class.

_about: What people want and CANNOT have — the highest-value row in the table.
The design table also lists 'architecture (allow-list, else other)'. It
is NOT here: the architecture string comes straight out of a
checkpoint's config.json (see cli.py:6122) and the engine holds no
allow-list to close it against, so shipping it would mean either a
free-form string (forbidden by sec 1.5) or an invented enum. It lands
when a real allow-list exists; error_class already separates
unsupported_architecture from the other failure modes.

capability_rejected._about: Features people reach for that we do not have.

_about: Which models / APIs / clients carry real load, and how many installs hit
repeated failures. One event per local counter threshold crossing:
O(log n) events, no timing trail, no sampling. Read it as unique
installs that reached bucket >= N — never as a sum.

agent_configure_failed._about: _failed twin: same identifying props, all optional, plus error_class.

telemetry_opted_out._about: The cost of default-on, measured. Sent once, then silence.

telemetry_opted_in._about: The other half of the same measurement.
